fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Paul says, “…there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.” (1 Corinthians 11:19) Think of approved like a cookie that passes inspection and gets sealed in the box. The differences bring that out into the open, showing which of them are approved. Paul has just said he hears of divisions among them when they come together as a church (verse 18).

Yes. Jesus says, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood…” (1 Corinthians 11:25) A covenant is a binding agreement, and Jesus says this new one is in His blood. Paul ties the cup to Jesus' death: as often as they eat the bread and drink the cup, they proclaim the Lord's death until He comes (verse 26). And Jesus says to do it in remembrance of Him.

Paul doesn't say honor. He says anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body “…eats and drinks judgment on himself.” (1 Corinthians 11:29) Jesus said of the bread, “This is My body, which is for you…” (verse 24), so I think recognizing the body means seeing what that bread is. Just before this, Paul says each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup (verse 28). Skip that, and the result is judgment, not honor.

problems.problem: The explanation still repeats that the differences show who is approved without explaining it.
The sentences after the quote restate the sequence without explaining the new covenant in Jesus’ blood.
The explanation discusses examining oneself but does not explain what recognizing the body means.
